messages:
alex: quick question — during the canary I noticed sampled logs for /v1/embeddings contain raw client text. expected?

devin: ugh, yeah that route bypassed the request-scrubber last week when we swapped serializers. only debug routes were supposed to include bodies.

mike: we intentionally left embeddings raw because downstream analytics needs exact tokenization for sharding. that was short-term tech debt.

tess: proposal: force a route-level scrub pipeline for embeddings and other vector payloads. store only salted-hash, token_count, and length metadata in logs. no raw text ever in sampled telemetry.

alex: strong +1. we need this to be default for hosted customers. enterprise allowlist can opt into inspect mode (see UX notes).

devin: implementation sketch: sampler should run scrub hooks before envelope creation. pseudoconfig:
```yaml
routes:
  "POST /v1/embeddings":
    sampling: 
      debug_percent: 0.01
      scrub_pipeline: [remove_pii, embed_hash, keep_lengths]
    allow_unmask: false
```

mike: question: salted hash will break dedupe across tenants. Is that okay? analytics uses cross-tenant dedupe today for anomaly detection.

tess: acceptable tradeoff. we can provide opt-in shared-hash for internal analytics teams under strict access controls, but normal logs should use tenant-specific salt.

security-bot: note: any unmask/unredact operation MUST create an audit entry with actor, justification, and TTL. KMS access required for per-tenant salts.

alex: acceptance criteria for rollout: 
- sampled logs for embeddings contain zero raw text for 99.999% of events
- unmask ops require manual justification + TTL and visible in audit logs
- console shows masked/unmasked counts per-tenant

tess: console UX items: 
- new "Inspect" toggle: default off. turning on shows only hashed values.
- "Unmask for X minutes" button: modal requires reason and 2FA. unmask TTL is recorded.
- heatmap on telemetry page showing "masked ratio" by route and time.

devin: telemetry TODOs: emit metric `logs.masked_ratio` per route, `unmask.requests` with outcome codes, and `emb.hash_collisions` (rare) — set alert if collisions > 0.01%

mike: rollout plan idea: canary at 1% host-level with feature flag `force_scrub_embeddings` -> 10% after 48h if no regressions -> 100% after perf verification. include a canary query param `?raw_debug=true` that only works for our internal tenants behind a gate.

tess: perf note: scrub pipeline adds small CPU cost; plan to implement in worker pool (async) before write to log stream to avoid latency spikes.

ops-bot: scheduled deploy: feature/emb-scrub -> canary cluster at 2028-05-02T03:00Z, rollback window 60m.

devin: I'll open PR with config + unit tests + integration test that simulates embeddings payload containing email/ssn and asserts no plaintext ends up in logs.

alex: add to runbook: how to respond if a customer claims missing raw text for analytics — steps to request temporary unmask (approval flow) and how to run impact analysis without exposing PII.

mike: one more: embeddings sent from mobile SDKs sometimes include screenshot OCR text in params. we should update ingest docs to remind SDKs to client-side scrub sensitive fields before sending.

tess: agreed. doc blurb + SDK lint rule.

alex: ok looks like we have consensus. devin, tag me on the PR and security for approval. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

devin: will do, drafting now :eyes:
